coverage_note: Whole file read. Lesson = N-verb drill (بنزعج / بنبسط / بنكسر) after a short chat about the weekend and the date/clothes/weather intro. Skipped as S4 pronunciation: 05:17 هدرت/هدرتها for حضرت (Amal 05:22 حضرتها), 19:03 'n-nitlab' for نلعب (Amal 19:06 نلعب), 53:16 انبسينا for انبسطنا (Amal 'you missed a letter'), 26:43 shadda on بسّط (filed low as B12/F3). Skipped as self-fix before her (GR-22): 02:42 خل-- خلاص, 30:06 ما تنزعجش -> ما تنزعجي مني, 23:22 بنطلون -> شورت, 54:38 بيبسط -> بيبسطوا, 42:16 aju -> Ajitu (Amal only echoed أجيتوا). 02:06 'أشتري في محلي' = engine for بشتغل (chat 03:41 bashte8el fi ma7alli); no voiced signal, not written. 28:20 Medi زعجني, Amal 28:22 'أزعجني' = engine/echo, chat 29:11 huwwe za3ajni confirms his form, not a slip. 1:01:58 'بكم مرة؟ Sorry.' right after Amal spoke = kaman marra? (not a slip). 14:03 'قبل ما تصلحي شو' - Amal asked for the illi version; chat 15:41 gives both 'illi kasartih / shu kasarti', question about the rule, not a slip. 47:50 'they made us happy would be بسطونا' was him checking the task, not a sentence. Echo candidates: 39:50 'I am happy.', 42:39 'I got happy?', 53:50 'Ah, shit.', 10:10 'Ah, oops.' are real English, not Arabic sound-alikes. Name امريكا (06:20) left alone. 'football' (04:45) and 'players/teams' (06:55, 07:16) are not on amal-sheet.txt, so no tier-3 rows; players/teams/interrupt written as didn't-know (tier 0). Repeat of a fixed line not re-scored: 06:52 اختارنا, 16:38 El Sadeeki, 34:00 تزعجنا, 52:18 انبسطوا, 1:01:16 بـ عزومة. English-only stretches: 21:01-22:06 (repetition talk), 27:44-28:10 (Meet dropout), 43:57-45:38 (Medi away), 51:04-51:35.

rows.amal_said: اشتريت؟ ... Oh، I thought you said اليوم اشتريت بيتي.
rows.why: He meant 'today I am working at home' but said بشتري (I buy); Amal heard 'I bought my house' and asked اشتريت؟ / said مبروك, he then fixed to اشتغلت and at 01:47 بشتغل في بيتي.
rows.english: Today I am working at my house.

rows.medi_said: واختارت، ... اختارت أضل... Is it خ-- what is it?
rows.amal_said: اخترت. ما فتاك، اخترت. (engine wrote اشتريت) ... Mhm. Some people say اخترت، they add E to make it easier.
rows.chat: u ana e5taret adall fi baiti
rows.why: Past 'I chose' came out as e5taarat; he asked 'what is it?', Amal gave e5taret (engine wrote اشتريت for her) but then said both ways are said - low because she accepted his form with Mhm.
rows.english: and I chose to stay at my house

rows.why: 'stay at my house' needs the preposition في; he dropped it and Amal recast في بيتي, he repeated.
rows.english: I chose to stay at my house.

rows.medi_said: في المحل. [ضحكة] في الـ، في البيت.
rows.why: Answering 'do you like working at home or at the shop' (her بالبيت ... بالمحل) he said في البيت and she recast بالبيت, typed belbait; low because في البيت is also fine and she may just be re-phrasing.

rows.medi_said: موظفيني، uh، interrupts me. I don't know how to say interrupt.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked how to say 'interrupt'; Amal supplied بيقاطعوني (chat bey2aat3uni; the engine wrote بيعطوني). Not on amal-sheet.txt.

rows.chat: 3utleti awal lu3be amrikiyye lalmawsem u ana 7deretha
rows.why: لعبة is feminine so the adjective is amrikiyye (her chat); he said the masculine أمريكي and she let it pass on voice.

rows.medi_said: Uh، do you guys use fas-فصل for the same season like a, a sports season?
rows.amal_said: I would say موسم for this type of season. ... للموسم.
rows.why: Didn't-know: he asked whether فصل (sheet: season | Fasel | فصل) covers a sports season; Amal supplied موسم. A question, so tier 0.
'I enjoyed it a lot' is كتير (he said كتير at 05:38, her chat kteer); the repeat came out كبير (big) and Amal let it pass - may be the engine.

rows.medi_said: uh, uh، تـ uh ختارن اختارن اختارينا
rows.why: Past 'we chose' is e5tarna; he produced e5taarina and Amal recast اخترنا.
Didn't-know: he stopped at 'players' and Amal supplied لاعبين; not on amal-sheet.txt.
Past 'we made' is 3melna; he said 3melina and Amal recast عملنا.
Didn't-know: he had no word for team; Amal supplied فريق, plural فرق, فرقنا. Not on amal-sheet.txt.
She asked for the plural of اسم; he tried اسمه / اسمي and she supplied the broken plural أسماء.

rows.amal_said: It's different than English. We will say the nouns it's easy to remember them. So it's easy. We don't need to tie it back to أسماء. ... So just سهل to remember them.
rows.proposed_rule: 'X are easy to do' keeps sehel unchanged before the verb - el-asmaa2 sehel netzakkarhom - no plural or feminine ending on sehel to match the noun.
rows.why: He made 'easy' agree with the plural أسماء (سهلات); Amal explained the Arabic frame is 'the names, it is easy to remember them' with invariant سهل - no bucket covers this frame, A8/A9 agreement is the nearest.

rows.medi_said: remove the B, right? 'Cause it's to remember. So أتذكرهم.
rows.amal_said: صح. mm-hmm. So it's either you or we. 'Cause it's general. ... نتذكرهم.
rows.why: For a general statement she wanted the 'we' (or you) form netzakkarhom, not 'I'; low because she first said صح and offered it as a choice.
'one of the homeworks' needs من (wa7ad min el-wajbaat); he dropped it and Amal only answered the number.
rows.english: I forgot one of the homeworks.

rows.medi_said: أنا لازم أعمله-- أم-أعملهم هون. ... هون؟ هلق, goddammit. I always mix up هلق and هون.
rows.why: He said هون (here) for 'now'; he caught it himself (هلق) in the same second Amal said هلا (sheet: now | Halla | هلا) - may be his own self-fix (GR-22), so low.
rows.english: I have to do them now.

rows.amal_said: You broke. You broke the thing that you have to fix. Not you were broken.
rows.chat: 2abel ma tsall7i illi kasartih / shu kasarti
rows.why: 'what you broke' needs the plain verb kasarti; he used the n- (get-broken) form enkasarti and Amal said 'not you were broken', he fixed to كسرتي.
'one of my friend's hands' takes the dual idain after wa7de min; he said the singular إيد, she prompted 'Hands.' and he fixed to إيدين.

rows.amal_said: Mm-hmm. صديقي. No L 'cause there's ي. ... Because it's صديقي، my friend، ما بحتاج L.
rows.why: A noun carrying the possessive ending -i never takes el-; he said el-sadeeqi twice (16:29, 16:38) and Amal named the rule.
The subject is one (feminine) hand, so the verb is enkasrat; he gave plural انكسروا then masculine انكسر before she got him to انكسرت.

rows.amal_said: We were playing. Where is the were? ... No، that would be played when we played. ... We took it with the used to.
rows.why: 'when we were playing' is kaan + present (kunna nel3ab); he used the simple past la3abna and Amal prompted for the 'were'.
Past 'we were' is kunna; he invented kunayna and Amal recast كنّا.

rows.medi_said: اليوم بلبس بلوزة أزرق و زرقا
rows.why: بلوزة is feminine so the colour is zar2a; he said the masculine أزرق, then زرقا in the same second Amal said it - treated as her recast, medium because it may be his own fix.
rows.english: Today I am wearing a blue blouse.

rows.why: Idafa: el- goes on the second word only (darajet el-7arara); he put it on the first and left the second bare, Amal recast.

rows.medi_said: بس في كاليفورنيا، uh عشان um عادةً um م-م-من شاف، من شاف؟ Try.

rows.english: But in California it is usually dry (so the heat is not bad).

rows.medi_said: المفضل لي-- or just مفضل لي. Right? No ال؟
rows.why: 'my favourite' is el-mufaddal 3indi; he used li- and Amal recast with عندي (and kept the el- he asked about).
Past of 'make happy' is bassat with the doubled middle; his basat lacked it and Amal echoed the stressed form - mostly sound shape (F3), so low.

rows.amal_said: شو بيزعجك؟ It's annoying you. مش...
rows.why: 'what annoys you' is the plain verb byez3ejak; he used the n- (get annoyed) form and Amal recast, he said 'there's no N'.

rows.amal_said: زعجناها. ... It's neither. It's just زعجنا. Only the I and you male take the it.
rows.why: 'maybe we annoyed her' is past za3ajna + -ha; he gave a present/you-form tez3ejna with no object ending and Amal recast زعجناها.

rows.amal_said: You annoy me. ... Yes, you guys annoy me. مش be annoyed by. ... بتزعجوني.
rows.why: 'you guys annoy me' is the plain verb btez3ejuni; he used the n- form and Amal said 'مش be annoyed by', he fixed to بتزعجوني.
'everyone gets annoyed by him' needs the n- form byenze3ej; he offered the plain بزعج, Amal prompted 'Gets annoyed.' and he fixed to بينزعج منه.
'enjoy your time' takes the -ak/-ek ending; he said بوقتي (my time), Amal prompted 'Your time.' and he fixed to wa'atik.
Her chat gives the feminine command enbes6i (she is the listener); he used the masculine انبسط and she said صح on voice, so unsignalled and low.
'did I make you happy' is past basattak; he gave the present ببسطك and Amal prompted ماضي, he moved to the past.
His past form came out without the -t- of 'I' (basatik); Amal recast بسطتك (chat basa6tek) - low because the engine may have dropped the t.
'I got happy' is the n- form enbasa6et; he gave بسطت (I made happy), Amal stopped him and he fixed to انبسطت at 42:55.

rows.amal_said: Mm, mm. في كمان. في إشي. ناقص. ... بس قهوتك. What does it need? ... بقهوتك.
rows.why: انبسط takes bi- before the thing enjoyed; he dropped it, Amal said something is missing and he produced بقهوتك.

rows.medi_said: Oh, you're back. Yeah, you're back. آه، أنا أرجع... برجع.
rows.amal_said: Mm-mm. رجعت. [تضحك] أنا رجعت. ... I came back.
rows.why: 'I am back' is said in the past (rje3et); he used the present برجع and Amal recast أنا رجعت.
'you get happy' is the n- form btenbes6i; he gave the make-happy form and Amal recast, he repeated Bitenbasti.
rows.english: You get happy when you go out.

rows.english: You guys should get happy more than this.

rows.medi_said: من، أكثر من، أكثر من هذا.

'enjoy the party' is انبسط بـ; he reached for مع and Amal recast بالحفلة.

rows.english: He enjoys your outings a lot.

rows.amal_said: Did she make you happy؟ ... did.

The subject is 'she' (her chat heyye) and the verb is feminine, but he said هو; Amal let it pass.
